## security-reviewer:input-validation:ae93c3cc

```yaml
blocker_id: security-reviewer:input-validation:ae93c3cc
section_anchor: executable-contributions
reviewer_count: 1
```

**Reviewer:** security-reviewer

```
SEC-1 — blocker — input-validation — Executable contributions, bound 2, L163-165.

THIS SPEC: "No contributed command is ever passed to `sh -c`", justified by `merge-gates.mjs:34-38`.

CONFLICTS WITH: `lib/gates/doctor.mjs:963` does exactly that — `spawnSync("sh", ["-c", command], { cwd: projectRoot })` — on a value `loadGates` (:1109-1133) reads straight out of `gates.yaml`, filtering only `g && typeof g === "object"`. It never goes through `mergeGates`, so the cited enforcement is not in that path at all. The project's own `gates.yaml:29` still carries `command: "npm test"`, a shell string, which proves the doctor path accepts what `mergeGates` rejects.

What actually keeps a contributed argv inert there is `normaliseCommand` (`doctor.mjs:254-268`) plus `NEEDS_QUOTING` (:219 — [\s'"&|;<>()$`*?[\]!#~=%\\]), which single-quotes every metacharacter-bearing token with POSIX '\'' escaping. The failure mode without it was verified empirically: `spawnSync("sh", ["-c", ["node","x$(id -u > /tmp/PWNED_ADEV)"]])` coerces the array to `node,x$(id -u > /tmp/PWNED_ADEV)` and the substitution EXECUTES (the file was created). So the safety of rule 2 rests entirely on a quoting function this spec never names, under `--execute` (opt-in, `doctor.mjs:739-749`).

RECOMMENDATION: Restate rule 2 as "argv-array only at the contribution boundary; the one shell executor, `doctor.mjs:963`, is safe because `normaliseCommand`/`NEEDS_QUOTING` shell-quote every token," and declare that quoting a dependency of Invariant 6 exactly as the spec already does for `lib/diagnostics/index.mjs`, with a matching acceptance criterion pinning it (mirroring L407). Do not leave a security bound justified by a claim the cited code contradicts.
```

## security-reviewer:path-traversal:3c03040e

```yaml
blocker_id: security-reviewer:path-traversal:3c03040e
section_anchor: executable-contributions
reviewer_count: 1
```

**Reviewer:** security-reviewer

```
SEC-2 — blocker — path-traversal — Executable contributions, bound 1, L156-162.

THIS SPEC: every argv element naming a path must resolve inside the extension's installed directory, verified with resolve() + startsWith + realpathSync.

CONFLICTS WITH: the spec never says what a RELATIVE argv element resolves against. Install-time it implies `resolvedPath`; at run time nothing re-resolves anything — `quality-gate.mjs:44-52` does `execFile(executable, args, { cwd: ctx.cwd })` and the doctor uses `cwd: projectRoot`. A relative argv path therefore resolves against the PROJECT ROOT when it executes, not the extension directory it was validated against. An extension declaring `[bash, bin/check.sh]` passes containment at install and runs `<projectRoot>/bin/check.sh` — a file the extension does not control.

Worse, for npm/git sources `resolvedPath` is a `mkdtempSync` temp dir that `installExtension`'s `finally` block deletes (`install.mjs:178-183`, `resolve-source.mjs:127/147/171/194`), and nothing anywhere copies extension executables into the project (`content-install.mjs` writes only to `domains/`, `governance/`, `samples/`, `skill-extensions/`). So for every non-local source, a path that satisfies rule 1 is GUARANTEED not to exist at execution. The capability rev 4 says it is preserving does not function. The spec also does not define behavior when the mandated `realpathSync` throws ENOENT.

RECOMMENDATION: Pick one and specify it: (a) copy the extension's executable payload into a project-owned, installer-controlled directory (e.g. `.context-index/extensions/<name>/`) at install time and rewrite argv paths to that absolute location, so install-time containment and run-time resolution share a base; or (b) require argv paths to be absolute and rooted at that installed directory. Either way, state the base directory explicitly, state that `realpathSync` failure is a refusal (`GOVERNANCE_COMMAND_ESCAPES_EXTENSION`), and realpath the BASE as well as the candidate (macOS /var→/private/var defeats a raw startsWith).
```

SA-3 — blocker — unsatisfiable precondition — Executable contributions, bound 1, L156-162; Acceptance Criteria L400-401.

THIS SPEC: bound 1 pins argv paths to "the extension's installed directory — `resolvedPath`, the first argument to `installExtension`".

CONFLICTS WITH: for npm and git sources `resolvedPath` is inside a `mkdtempSync` temp dir (`lib/extensions/resolve-source.mjs:127,171`) that `installExtension`'s own `finally` block deletes (`lib/extensions/install.mjs:179-182`); for local sources it is an arbitrary path outside the project. Nothing in `content-install.mjs` copies an extension's `bin/` anywhere — it writes only `domains/`, `governance/`, `samples/`, `skill-extensions/`. So a command satisfying bound 1 points at a directory that no longer exists when the gate runs. Conversely the reference extension's `[bash, extensions/example-validation-check/bin/check.sh]` is a repo-relative path resolved at `cwd` = consumer repo root (`lib/governance/quality-gate.mjs:49`, `doctor.mjs:966`); it does not resolve inside `resolvedPath`, so the claim that it "satisfies this unchanged" (L162) is false and acceptance criteria L400 ("installs successfully unchanged") and L401 are mutually exclusive.

RECOMMENDATION: Name the durable containment root explicitly and specify how the extension's executable gets there (a content-install copy step, or containment to the project root plus a distinct rule), then re-check the reference extension against it. See SEC-2 for the run-time half of the same defect.
